title: Azure Data Factory Pipeline Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.50 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.50 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="PipelineRuns"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.50_azure_data_factory_pipel_50"
| sort -_time
description: Data Factory orchestrates ETL/ELT pipelines that feed data warehouses, analytics, and operational systems. Pipeline failures cause stale data, broken dashboards, and missed SLAs.
value: Detecting azure data factory pipeline failures early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable diagnostics on Data Factory to route `PipelineRuns`, `ActivityRuns`, and `TriggerRuns` to Splunk via Event Hub. Alert on failed pipeline runs. Track activity-level errors for root cause (copy failures, data flow errors, linked service timeouts). Monitor pipeline duration trending to detect degradation before SLA breach.
visualization: Table (failed pipelines with error), Bar chart (failures by pipeline), Line chart (pipeline duration trend).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable diagnostics on Data Factory to route `PipelineRuns`, `ActivityRuns`, and `TriggerRuns` to Splunk via Event Hub. Alert on failed pipeline runs. Track activity-level errors for root cause (copy failures, data flow errors, linked service timeouts). Monitor pipeline duration trending to detect degradation before SLA breach.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="PipelineRuns"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.50_azure_data_factory_pipel_50"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:diagnostics` in `index=cloud` to detect azure data factory pipeline failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_50_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (failed pipelines with error), Bar chart (failures by pipeline), Line chart (pipeline duration trend)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure data factory pipeline failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
